title: Scanner signal enrichment and priority heuristics (proto)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype doc that captures the proposed approach for enriching raw scanner signals (OSS dependency scanners, SAST, container scanners) into SIEM-friendly events and a lightweight priority heuristic that ties to patch SLAs and RBAC v2 evidence automation flows. Goal: improve triage signal-to-noise and create deterministic routing for remediation owners and evidence capture.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Normalization strategy for scanner outputs (common fields, severity mapping, fingerprinting)
- Enrichment sources (SBOM, repo metadata, ownership, runtime telemetry)
- Priority heuristic design (score components, weights, thresholds)
- SIEM export schema tweaks and RBAC v2 tag propagation
- Evidence automation hooks for remediation workflows and SLA tracking
- Example flows for dependency vs. code findings

Notes / context:
- We currently receive scanner outputs from three primary pipelines: deps-checker (OSS), container-scanner (images), and static-analyzer (monorepo SAST). Each pipeline emits different JSON shapes and severity semantics.
- Problem: triage teams see many noisy, duplicate, or low-actionable alerts — slows down SLA adherence. We want consistent scoring and confidence so auto-routing/auto-ack can be used for low-risk items.

Normalization (proto fields to standardize):
- id (string): canonical vuln id (prefer CVE if present, else composite id: scanner|hash)
- source (string): scanner name (deps-checker, clair, semgrep)
- raw_severity (string): original scanner severity
- severity (string): normalized -> critical|high|medium|low|info
- confidence (string): low|medium|high (scanner-provided or inferred)
- fingerprint (string): deterministic fingerprint for dedupe (component + path + signature)
- component (string): package/module name or binary
- version (string): impacted version(s)
- manifest_path (string): repo path or image tag
- evidence_links (list): array of evidence artifacts (scan report ids, diffs)
- first_seen, last_seen (dates)

Severity mapping (initial rules):
- CVE with CVSS >= 9.0 -> critical
- CVE CVSS 7.0-8.9 -> high
- Known exploit in the wild -> bump +1 severity tier
- Outdated package + no upstream fix -> high/critical depending on CVSS
- semgrep pattern matches without exploitability metadata -> medium/low

Enrichment sources and methods:
- SBOM lookup: map component -> commit repo, maintainer, release cadence. If SBOM shows component in prod runtime clusters, boost severity by 1 for critical infra components.
- Ownership resolution: link manifest_path -> CODEOWNERS / repo metadata -> produce owner email/groups. If no owner, tag `unowned` and route to infra-security queue.
- Runtime telemetry: if the component is observed in production via telemetry (runtime-asset-index), raise confidence score.
- Dependency graph context: check whether vulnerable component is reachable from top-level app package (direct vs transitive). Direct dependency weight +2.

Priority heuristic (scoring):
- Base severity score: critical=100, high=70, medium=40, low=15, info=0
- Exploitability modifier: +25 if exploit known in public exploit-db or hunter feed
- Production exposure modifier: +20 if seen in runtime telemetry, +10 if present in staging only
- Ownership modifier: +0 if owner present, +15 if unowned (to escalate to triage)
- Dependency depth modifier: +15 if direct dependency, +5 if transitive depth 1, 0 if depth >1
- Age modifier: +10 if first_seen > 90 days (stale findings)
- Confidence multiplier: high*1.0, medium*0.85, low*0.6

Final priority = (sum of components) * confidence_multiplier -> normalized to 0-100. Thresholds: >85 urgent (24h SLA), 60-85 high (3d SLA), 30-60 medium (14d SLA), <30 low (next sprint).

SIEM export schema notes (fields to add/update):
- event_type: vulnerability.alert
- vuln_id: id (canonical)
- priority_score: integer 0-100
- assigned_team: resolved team or `unowned`
- assigned_user: user email (if auto-assigned via CODEOWNERS)
- evidence_refs: list of evidence ids (for playbook links)
- rbac_tags: list (rbac:v2 tags e.g., project:payments, env:prod, owner-team:platform)
- action_suggested: triage|patch|mitigate|ignore (initial suggestion based on policy)

RBAC v2 propagation and evidence automation hooks:
- When ownership is resolved, add rbac_tags to SIEM event so downstream Splunk/QRadar dashboards can filter by team.
- Evidence automation: when a finding enters `patch` state, create an evidence bundle: patch-runbook.md (template), scan-diff, patch-PR link, SRE post-deploy check checklist. Store bundle id in evidence_refs.
- Evidence retention: keep snapshot of scan artifacts and SBOM lines for 180 days (for audit).

Routing / automation rules (proto):
- Priority >85 and assigned_team present -> create Jira ticket (SEC-CRITICAL queue), assign to owner, set SLA 24h. Auto-add playbook template.
- 60-85 & owner present -> create ticket (SEC-HIGH), SLA 72h.
- Unowned & priority >60 -> create ticket in infra-safety-scan, assign to rotation on-call.
- Priority <30 and confidence low -> auto-suppress for 90 days with re-eval cadence.

Example flows (dependency finding):
- deps-checker reports CVE-2024-xxxx in package `yaml-parser` used by `service-auth` (direct). SBOM shows package in prod clusters. Runtime telemetry confirms usage. Score: base high (70) + prod exposure (20) + direct (15) + age (0) = 105 -> cap 100 -> urgent. Route to `service-auth` owner. Create Jira SEC ticket with evidence bundle and SLA 24h.

Example flows (SAST finding):
- semgrep match flagged potential SQL injection in legacy-handler. Confidence medium. Not present in runtime telemetry -> medium priority. Assign to repo owner with 14d SLA and recommended mitigation steps in playbook.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should auto-suppression be? Risk of missing slow-moving exploit campaigns vs reducing noise. Suggested: conservative for first 3 months; use manual overrides.
- Fingerprint stability: we need a robust fingerprint algorithm to avoid churn across scanners and sensor upgrades. Prototype: sha256(component+path+normalized-stack-signature).
- RBAC tagging fidelity: CODEOWNERS often incomplete. Add heuristics (recent committers, last reviewer) to guess owner but mark as `probable` not authoritative.

Operational runbook (short):
- On new scanner schema onboard: add mapping to normalization layer (lambda) + unit tests for severity mapping.
- Daily job: de-dup and merge new findings into existing issues (merge by fingerprint); update last_seen.
- Weekly: review auto-suppressed findings and re-evaluate with updated threat-intel feeds.

Action items (owners):
- Marco: build normalization prototype lambda and mapping table (due 2026-05-01)
- Evelyn: draft SIEM field mapping and Splunk query examples (due 2026-05-08)
- Samir: prototype ownership resolution using CODEOWNERS + recent committers heuristic (due 2026-05-10)
- Priya: write evidence bundle template and retention policy note (due 2026-05-05)

Next steps / milestones:
- Spike to run normalization on a 2-week scan backlog and generate scores -> measure reduction in triage volume and SLA meet rate (due 2026-05-20)
- Present results at security weekly (2026-05-25) and iterate thresholds

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- add example SIEM JSON payloads -> (TODO)
- include sample Jira automation recipe for SEC queues -> (TODO)
- sync with SRE on runtime telemetry feed availability (Slack: #infra-observability)

References:
- Confluence: Scan Normalization Design (linked above)
- SEC-4123: dependency-ownership-heuristics
- GH-3142: evidence-bundle-template PR

Draft status: rough prototype. Heavy on heuristics — will need tuning after running against historical data. Keep discussion here and we will move to design doc if the spike results are promising.
